_comment: Status overlay for the implementation tracker. backlog.json owns the stories and their acceptance criteria; this file owns delivery status, the abridged title shown in the tracker, and phase alignment. Regenerate the page with `npm run tracker`. test/tracker.spec.ts fails if the two files fall out of sync.

spec_phases.name: Foundation
spec_phases.focus: Canonical model, one shared state machine, basic RBAC

spec_phases.name: Signal
spec_phases.focus: Aging and SLA engine, git and CI/CD integration, team dashboards

spec_phases.name: Traceability
spec_phases.focus: Lineage graph, monitoring integration, notification and escalation

spec_phases.name: Scale & governance
spec_phases.focus: CMDB federation, chatops, analytics suite, enterprise hardening

US1.1.name: One shared WorkItem schema
US1.1.note: Verified by test/us1.1.spec.ts — four canonical types, stable keys, 422 on unknown type.

US1.2.name: Filtered views, scoped to tenant
US1.2.note: Verified by test/us1.2.spec.ts — state and aging filters, cross-tenant reads denied.

US1.3.name: Per-type custom fields
US1.3.note: Verified by test/us1.3.spec.ts — JSON-schema validation and documented defaults.

US2.1.name: Configurable workflow definitions
US2.1.note: Verified by test/us2.1.spec.ts — versioned publish, in-flight items keep their version.

US2.3.name: Integration-triggered transitions
US2.3.note: Verified by test/us2.3.spec.ts — a guard-rejected external transition is skipped and logged, never forced.

US3.1.name: Business-calendar thresholds
US3.1.note: Verified by test/us3.1.spec.ts — 5×8 excludes weekends; no policy means no false alert.

US3.2.name: Continuous aging score
US3.2.note: Verified by test/us3.2.spec.ts — green below 75%, amber to 100%, red beyond, on a 60-second tick.

US3.3.name: Warning and breach events
US3.3.note: Verified by test/us3.3.spec.ts — SLAWarning at 75%, SLABreached at 100%, with recipients.

US3.4.name: SLA clock suspension on hold
US3.4.note: New from research §3. Time in a hold state such as Waiting for Customer must not consume SLA budget.

US4.1.name: Typed link creation
US4.1.note: Verified by test/us4.1.spec.ts — edges validated per type pair, invalid pairs rejected with the allowed list.

US4.2.name: Upstream lineage query
US4.2.note: Verified by test/us4.2.spec.ts — upstream and downstream follow relationship semantics, not one traversal twice.

US4.3.name: Service impact analysis
US4.3.note: Verified by test/us4.3.spec.ts — depth-bounded walk from a Service returning the edge chain implicating each item.

US4.4.name: Exportable lineage report
US4.4.note: No export endpoint exists. Lineage is queryable as JSON but cannot be emitted as an audit artefact.

US5.1.name: Schema-registered domain events
US5.1.note: Events are persisted to domain_events on a datastore that survives a restart, queryable at GET /events, and the org_id addition to WorkItemStateChanged was additive as the story requires. Still partial: the write happens just after the mutation rather than inside its transaction, so the outbox guarantee is unmet.

US5.2.name: Idempotent event processing
US5.2.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — EventConsumerRegistry keys consumption on (consumer, event_id), so a redelivery is a no-op for every registered consumer rather than only where a service hand-rolled it.

US5.3.name: Dead-letter queue with alerting
US5.3.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — a handler is retried to its configured limit, then written to dead_letter_events with its payload, attempts and error, and a DeadLetterQueueAlert fires carrying the depth.

US5.4.name: HTTP 202 asynchronous ingestion
US5.4.note: New from research §4. Webhooks are processed synchronously today, the classic webhook-timeout failure mode at volume.

US5.5.name: Dead-letter replay console
US5.5.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — GET /dlq, inline payload correction and POST /dlq/:id/replay preserving the original event id, plus discard. A failed replay stays queued rather than being lost.

US6.1.name: Commit and PR auto-linking
US6.1.note: Verified by test/us6.1.spec.ts — keys extracted from messages; unreferenced commits still stored.

US6.2.name: Merged PR advances its story
US6.2.note: Verified by test/us6.2.spec.ts — runs through the workflow engine as an integration actor.

US6.3.name: Deployment to release traceability
US6.3.note: Verified by test/us6.3.spec.ts — links stories and releases, advances the release, replays idempotently.

US7.1.name: Alert-driven incident creation
US7.1.note: Verified by test/us7.1.spec.ts — SEV1–SEV4 mapping, Triaged on create, rolling dedupe window.

US7.2.name: Affected-service linking
US7.2.note: Verified by test/us7.2.spec.ts — affects edge to the Service registry; Services are not WorkItems.

US7.3.name: Mitigation proposed, never forced
US7.3.note: Verified by test/us7.3.spec.ts — walks to Mitigated one guarded step at a time; never Resolved or Closed.

US8.1.name: SLA warning reaches the owner
US8.1.note: Routing, preference and audit log verified by test/us8.1.spec.ts. Channel transports are declared pilot stubs, so nothing is literally delivered.

US8.2.name: Breach and escalation routing
US8.2.note: Owner plus team lead on breach, configured target at 150%, verified by test/us8.2.spec.ts. Same transport boundary.

US8.3.name: Channel choice with email fallback
US8.3.note: Preference, fallback and failure recording verified by test/us8.3.spec.ts. Same transport boundary.

US9.1.name: Team aging heatmap
US9.1.note: The board colours by aging bucket and sorts worst-first, and renders under browser test, but the ordering itself is not asserted.

US9.2.name: Cross-team executive rollup
US9.2.note: No SLA compliance, cycle time or aging distribution per team or business unit.

US9.3.name: Interactive traceability explorer
US9.3.note: Lineage renders as a linear chain, not an expandable graph.

US9.4.name: DORA and ITIL metrics
US9.4.note: Verified by test/us9.4.spec.ts — deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore, all derived from recorded history. Change failure rate comes from the Incident caused_by Release edge and ships with the deployment/incident pairs behind it.

US10.1.name: SSO login
US10.1.note: Not implemented. The research playbook records this as complete; it is not.

US10.2.name: SCIM provisioning
US10.2.note: Not implemented. The research playbook records this as complete; it is not.

US10.3.name: Role-gated transitions
US10.3.note: Verified by test/us10.3.spec.ts — role resolution against the people table gates every transition.

US10.4.name: Audit-trail export
US10.4.note: Every transition writes an immutable audit_events row, but no export endpoint exposes them.

US10.5.name: Identity by immutable account id
US10.5.note: New from research §8. Email-based lookup breaks silently when profile visibility hides the address.

US10.6.name: Deactivation via SCIM PATCH
US10.6.note: New from research §8. The target REST API has no deactivation endpoint, so deprovisioning must go through SCIM.

US11.1.name: Federated Service/Asset source
US11.1.note: The Service registry is local. Nothing reads from an authoritative external CMDB, and there is no staleness flag.

US11.2.name: Incidents linked to the correct CI
US11.2.note: Incidents link to Services with an owning team, but alert-discovered entries are local stubs flagged monitoring_discovery.

US13.1.name: ITIL to Agile state matrix
US13.1.note: Configurable translation so each platform shows its own native lifecycle; an unmapped state holds for review rather than guessing.

US13.2.name: Immutable correlation references
US13.2.note: Each side stores the other's immutable id, so the pair survives renames and re-indexing without summary-text matching.

US13.3.name: Echo-loop suppression
US13.3.note: Self-originated webhooks identified by service-account identity plus payload hash, with content comparison as the fallback after a restart.

US13.4.name: Work-note privacy in comment sync
US13.4.note: Comment sync opt-in by default; internal work notes never reach a customer-visible stream.

US13.5.name: Resolution code write-back
US13.5.note: Closure metadata written back so ITIL records stay complete without manual re-entry.

US14.1.name: Format-preserving transfer
US14.1.note: Parse source HTML to an intermediate tree, then serialise to the target's document format or wiki markup from the same representation.

US14.2.name: Inline media and attachments
US14.2.note: Screenshots transfer as attachments referenced at their original positions; oversized files warn and link back rather than failing the record.

US15.1.name: Incident-storm duplicate detection
US15.1.note: Embedding similarity above the configured threshold suppresses the duplicate and links it under a master incident.

US15.2.name: Stack-trace entity extraction
US15.2.note: Component and affected version inferred from logs, flagged machine-derived, left unset below the confidence threshold.

US15.3.name: CAB release risk scoring
US15.3.note: Score from historical velocity, prior change-failure rate and blast radius; high scores route to an elevated approval tier.

US16.1.name: Adaptive rate governance
US16.1.note: Shape outbound calls inside each target's quota and honour Retry-After instead of failing at the boundary.

US16.2.name: Indexed-query safety
US16.2.note: Reject queries against unindexed fields at configuration time; shed load rather than retrying into semaphore exhaustion.

US16.3.name: Zero-inbound-port connectivity
US16.3.note: A relay behind the firewall long-polls over outbound HTTPS, so integrating never widens the attack surface.
